title: U.S. House · Alabama's 1st Congressional District
area: Southwest Alabama, including Mobile and Baldwin counties along the Gulf Coast.

context.text: This is an open seat. Incumbent Barry Moore (R), who won the redrawn District 1 in 2024, ran for the U.S. Senate in 2026 instead of seeking re-election here. A new congressional map, signed into law after the Supreme Court's Louisiana v. Callais ruling, moved this district's primary to August 11, 2026; the primary originally scheduled for May 19 was voided. Former U.S. Representative Jerry Carl, who represented this district from 2021 to 2025 before losing a 2024 primary to Moore, won the August 11 Republican primary. Clyde Jones advanced from the Democratic primary without opposition.

candidates.name: Jerry Carl
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary over Austin Sidwell, John Mills, and Lucas Burger.
candidates.currentRole: Former U.S. Representative for Alabama's 1st Congressional District (2021–2025)

summary.text: Jerry Carl is a Mobile-based entrepreneur who represented Alabama's 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2021 to 2025, before losing a 2024 primary against fellow incumbent Barry Moore after redistricting merged their districts. He is running to reclaim the seat, campaigning as an ally of President Trump on immigration, gun rights, and reduced federal spending.

background.text: Born in Mobile, Alabama; founded businesses in real estate, healthcare, and timber before entering politics.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2020 and re-elected in 2022; served on the House Committee on Appropriations and the House Committee on Armed Services during his time in Congress.

priorities.text: Says he will continue to work alongside President Trump's agenda in Congress.
Emphasizes border security, citing his prior vote for border-wall funding and hiring more Border Patrol agents.
Says Washington needs to "live within its means" and supports a Balanced Budget Amendment to the Constitution.
priorities.quote: Washington needs to live within its means, just like families and small-businesses do every day.

positions.summary: Campaign website says he worked in Congress to pass border security legislation, including wall funding and more Border Patrol agents, and will continue to prioritize border enforcement.
Describes himself as a lifelong Second Amendment supporter with a 100% rating from Gun Owners of America and a past NRA-Political Victory Fund endorsement.
Says he is "100% pro-life," opposes taxpayer funding for abortion, and supported the Supreme Court's decision overturning Roe v. Wade.
Says he opposes defunding the police and has been a strong supporter of law enforcement in Congress.
Says he stands with Israel and introduced legislation intended to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Appropriations (Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration; Financial Services and General Government; State Department, Foreign Operations subcommittees) in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

Served on the House Committee on Armed Services (Military Personnel; Seapower and Projection Forces subcommittees) and as Vice Ranking Member of the Natural Resources Committee's Water, Oceans, and Wildlife Subcommittee in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

candidates.name: Clyde Jones
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed.

summary.text: Clyde Jones is a retired U.S. Army veteran (1984–2005), Baptist minister, and the Democratic nominee for Alabama's 1st Congressional District, running on Medicaid expansion, congressional accountability, and immigration reform.

background.text: Served 21 years in the U.S. Army Signal Corps (1984–2005), retiring as a First Sergeant; received the Bronze Star Medal for service in Operation Desert Storm and Operation Iraqi Freedom II.
Earned a high school diploma from Charles City High School (Virginia) and a bachelor's degree from Excelsior University in 2008.
Retired from FMC Agriculture Solutions as a Process Safety Management Coordinator in May 2024; serves as an Associate Minister at Macedonia Missionary Baptist Church in Daphne, Alabama.

Served two years as President of the Board of Directors for the nonprofit Alabama Arise and sits on the Steering Committee for Leadership Baldwin and the Executive Committee for the Commission on Social Justice and Racial Reconciliation of the Episcopal Diocese of the Gulf Coast.

priorities.text: Says Congress should be accountable to voters rather than party leadership or the White House, and calls for total government transparency.
priorities.quote: Leadership matters! Congress needs to remember who they work for-not their party, not the White House, but the people in their district. I'll make certain their voices are heard and their needs are addressed, starting on day one.

priorities.text: Wants comprehensive healthcare coverage for all Alabamians.
priorities.quote: Comprehensive healthcare for all. No exceptions and nobody left behind. Hard working taxpayers of Alabama should never have to fear financial ruin from a health emergency.

priorities.text: Says his campaign will not take corporate PAC money and supports congressional reforms such as banning stock trading by members of Congress and their families and imposing term limits.
priorities.quote: I'll support and vote to overturn Citizens United, and get Corporate PACs out of our elections. In Congress I'll advocate and vote for a ban on stock trading for members and their immediate families.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicaid in Alabama and extending ACA Enhanced Premium Tax Credits, and backs a federal proposal to create a direct federal Medicare-style coverage program for residents of states, including Alabama, that continue to refuse Medicaid expansion.
positions.quote: I believe in the expansion of Medicaid, and ACA Enhanced Premium Tax Credits to ease the burden of health care on every day Americans.

positions.summary: Supports a path to documentation for undocumented immigrants and says immigration enforcement should not separate families or rely on arrest quotas, while saying secure borders are still important.
positions.quote: I will fight for real immigration reform — a clear, straightforward path for undocumented people to get documented — because the people doing the work that holds our communities together deserve better than to live in fear. Secure borders are important, but lives and families shouldn't be put on the line to hit arrest quotas.

candidates.researchNotes: Ballotpedia's basic biography was supplemented with Clyde Jones's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (completed, contrary to an earlier note that he had not) and his campaign website's Issues page, which supply his background, priorities, and two documented positions here.
